comments.author: @tomzdrodowski
comments.text:
Greetings from Sweden!

Your documentary has touched me deeply and helped me reconsider my own plans.

I live on an island in the Baltic Sea, where I am planning to build a small village of 18–20 houses on approximately 5.5 hectares of forest land. My dream is to create an affordable, peaceful community where people can live with dignity.

Watching your documentary, seeing homeless families, people with disabilities, and others struggling just to survive, reminded me how fortunate we are to have a roof over our heads. Something we often take for granted.

And then we hear stories of enormous amounts of money being allocated to help homeless people, even in wealthy cities like Las Vegas, yet so many remain on the streets. It makes you wonder where our priorities are.

Your documentary has made me rethink my project. Perhaps only five houses should become permanent homes, with the others used seasonally. I also want to prevent uncontrolled subdivision and development.

But more importantly, I want my little village to become something beyond houses. A community where people care for one another, where those who have more can share with those who have less, and where we might even welcome someone who has nowhere else to go.

I understand why people are sometimes afraid to help strangers. We live in a world where trust can be difficult. But if fear stops us from helping, what kind of world are we creating?

We cannot save everyone, but perhaps each of us can help someone.

Thank you for this documentary. It has reminded me that building a better future isn’t only about buildings, money, or planning. It’s about remembering that we are all human beings, and nobody should be forgotten.

Perhaps we should stop asking only how much we can build and start asking how many people we can help.
